issue.title: Move the task-statuses.css vault snippet into bob-ledger-tools so custom checkbox statuses render without the snippet

task_type_fields.proposal: Move the vault CSS snippet `.obsidian/snippets/task-statuses.css` (186 lines; paints the custom task checkbox statuses `?` Blocked, `/` Pending, `*` Next, `-` cancelled in Live Preview, reading view and Tasks results) into bob-ledger-tools' `styles.css`, so every custom status box (including today's plain `?` that blocked-reason marks fall back to) renders without depending on a separately enabled vault snippet. Keep the selectors' specificity contract with the blocked-reason mark CSS (`body.bob-block-marks ...` must still win by specificity, never `!important`), then disable/remove the snippet from the vault's `appearance.json` `enabledCssSnippets` and update bob-plugins docs plus bob-cli docs/blocked-marks.md ("Plain `?` stays the snippet's job") and any vault-format docs that describe the snippet.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic bob-cli-ft deliberately left `task-statuses.css` in the vault ("moving task-statuses.css into the plugin" is listed as out of scope in plan 202611/blocked_reason_marks.md) and asked its visual_review phase (bob-cli-ft.8 note #3) to record the move as a follow-up. Marked rows already draw their whole box without the snippet, so the epic is complete without it; the move is a separate packaging change touching the vault, the plugin CSS, and docs.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by bob-cli-ft.8 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #3) as the plan-mandated follow-up of the Blocked-reason marks epic, which kept the snippet move out of scope.

payload.description: Proposing epic: Blocked-reason marks; its CSS must keep winning over the moved status CSS by specificity
